texts.preamble: Shri Chander Mohan Sachdeva vs Shri Chanda Babu on 30 January, 2016 In The Court Of Anoop Kumar Mendiratta, Judge, Mact-1, (Central), Delhi. Suit No.271/12 Unique Case Id No.02401C-0357742012 1. Shri Chander Mohan Sachdeva S/o Shri H.C. Sachdeva, R/o 543Sf, B-1 Block, Janakpuri, New Delhi. ......... Pe Versus 1. Shri Chanda Babu S/o Shri Wazir, R/o Village Khoh, Ps: Hafizganj, Bareilly, U.P. ...................(Driver) 2. Shri Ameer Shah S/o Shri Bazeer Shah, R/o Village Khoh, Ps: Hafizganj, Bareilly, Up. ................... (Owner) 3. Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd. 122/167, 1st Floor, Old Pmg Office, Civil Lines, Bareilly, Up - 243001 ........... .......Responden Date of Institution of the suit : 04.08.201 Arguments heard on : 27.01.201 Judgment pronounced on : 30.01.201 Suit No.271/12 - Chander Mohan Sachdeva vs. Chanda Babu & Ors. Judgment
texts.facts: 1. Present claim petition has been preferred by the petitioner u/s 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') claiming compensation of a sum of Rs.1,50,00,000/- in respect of accidental injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicular accident. 2. Brief facts of the case as mentioned in the claim petition are that on 07.12.2010, petitioner was going from Bareilly to Pilibhit in jeep bearing registration no. UP 25AT 0349 which was driven by Shri Chander Mohan Sachdeva vs Shri Chanda Babu on 30 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58035091/ 1 Respondent No.1 Chanda Babu at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner . The occupants of the jeep warned Respondent No.1 but he continued to drive in the same manner and at about 10:00PM when they were about 1 Km. away from PS: Hafizganj, Bareilly, UP, the jeep hit a tractor from behind. Consequently, petitioner sustained grievous injuries. Respondent No.1 fled away from the spot leaving behind the occupants of the jeep. Petitioner was taken to Shri Ganga Charan Hospital, Bareilly for treatment wherein he remained admitted from 08.12.2010 to 15.12.2010 and was thereafter further treated at Eshan Hospital, Bareilly from 15.12.2010 to 03.01.2011. Petitioner came back to Delhi and was treated at Medanta Hospital, Gurgaon from 08.01.2011 to 12.01.2011. Petitioner claims to have spent about Rs.6,00,000/- on his medical treatment. It is further the case of petitioner that he was earning Rs.1,00,000/- per month from his business and had to remain on bed rest for about 15 months due to grievous injuries sustained in the accident. Further, a sum of Rs.75,000/- was claimed towards attendant charges, Rs.1,00,000/- towards conveyance and Rs. 2,00,000/- towards special diet. 3. In the joint Written Statement filed on behalf of Respondent No.1/driver of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2/owner of the offending vehicle, it was submitted that petition is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed since the accident took place at Bareilley. It was further submitted that the petitioner concealed the true facts and had sustained the injuries due to his own fault and negligence. Further, the contents of the claim petition were disputed. In the Written Statement filed on behalf of the Insurance Company, it was submitted that the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation in case it is found that the driver or owner of the offending vehicle had violated the terms and conditions of the policy or the driving licence was found to be fake or fabricated or in case it is proved that the driver was not driving vehicle no. UP 25AT 0349 with the consent and permission of insured. The petition was stated to be bad for non- joinder of driver, owner and insurer of the tractor. The liability of the insurance company was denied on the ground that the accident never took place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle. It was also submitted that the insurance company was not liable since the injured was travelling in the jeep as a gratuitous passenger. However, it was admitted that the vehicle no. UP 25AT 0349 was insured for the period 12.01.2010 to 11.01.2011. The claim was further stated to be excessive and exaggerated. 4. On the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed for consideration by ld. Predecessor:- (iii) Relief. Shri Chander Mohan Sachdeva vs Shri Chanda Babu on 30 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58035091/ 2 5. In support of claim, petitioner examined himself as PW1. PW-1 Chander Mohan testified on the lines of the claim petition and proved copy of Election I-card (Ex.PW1/1), copy of driving licence (Ex.PW1/2), copy of discharge summary of three different hospitals (four pages-colly Mark X), copy of medical prescriptions and medical bills (62 sheets-colly Mark Y), copy of reimbursement of hospital (Ex.PW1/4), copy of Form ST-2 and sales tax registration certificate (Ex.PW1/5 colly), copy of ITRs for the years 2007-08, 2008-09, 2009-10 and 2010-11 (5 sheets-colly Mark Z), Income Tax Return for Assessment Year 2011-12 and its balance sheet (29 sheets-colly Ex.PW1/6), copy of written complaint dated 18.08.2011 made to Senior Superintendent of Police, Bareilley (Mark Z-1), certified copy of FIR, chargesheet and site plan (06 pages-Ex.PW1/8), copy of driving licence of Respondent No.1, registration certificate, permit, fitness, insurance policy of the offending vehicle (06 pages-Mark Z2), copy of the certificate issued by National Fire Service College along with statement of marks (02 sheets-Ex.PW1/10) and original disability certificate (Ex.PW1/11). During cross-examination, he deposed that he was rushed to Ganga Charan Hospital, Bareilly, UP and the family members reached the hospital on the next day of the accident. Further, the police officials reached the spot of accident and had accompanied him to the hospital. Police officials obtained thumb impressions on the papers and he remained admitted in Ganga Charan Hospital for one week and was thereafter shifted to Eshan Hospital, Bareilly, UP. He further clarified that the spot of accident was a single road without any divider and wide enough for passing of two trucks and a car simultaneously. At the time of accident he was seated along with the driver. He further stated that there was a trolley attached to the tractor with two reflectors on the rear side and had noticed the trolley for the first time at a distance of 60-70 yards. He further denied the suggestion that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the tractor trolley. It was further denied that the expenses were not incurred as claimed in the affidavit. In response to court question, it was further clarified by the petitioner that all the original documents of treatment were handed over to East West Assist TPA Pvt. Ltd. as he had taken a mediclaim policy and further in view of limited liability, only a sum of Rs.2,02,950/- was paid out of the medical bills of Rs.4,40,294/-. No evidence was led on behalf of the respondents despite opportunity. 6. I have heard arguments addressed on behalf of the petitioner as well as counsel for Insurance Company and perused the record. On the other hand, the same has been vehemently disputed by counsel for insurance company and it was submitted that there was no loss of income for the Assessment Year 2011-12 as the net income is Rs.5,58,382/- while for the preceding year the same was Rs.4,52,220/-. It was further contended that ITR for AY 2011-12 (FY 01.04.2010 to 31.03.2011) cannot be considered since the Return was filed after the accident and the income be assessed on the basis of ITR for the AY 2010-11 @ Rs.4,52,220/-.
texts.arguments: In Bimla Devi and Ors. V. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors., (2009) 13 SC 530, it was held that a petition u/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 the Claim Tribunal has to decide the negligence on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition. In New India Assurance Co. Ltd. V. Sakshi Bhutani & ors, MAC APP. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012 by Hon'ble Mr. Justice G.P. Mittal (Delhi High Court), it was observed that it has to be borne in mind that the Motor Vehicles Act does not envisage holding a trial for a petition preferred under Section 166 of the Act. Under Section 168 of the Act, a Claims Tribunal is enjoined to hold an inquiry to determine compensation which must appear to it to be just. Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal. Further in State of Mysore Vs. S.S. Makapur, 1993 (2) SCR 943, the Supreme Court held that the Tribunals exercising quasi-judicial functions are not courts and are not bound by strict rules of evidence. The relevant portion of the report is extracted hereunder: ".......that tribunals exercising quasi-judicial functions are not courts and that therefore they are not bound to follow the procedure prescribed for trial of actions in courts nor are they bound by strict rules of evidence. They can unlike courts, obtain all information for the points under the enquiry from all sources, and through all channels, without being fettered by rules and procedure, which govern proceedings in court. The only obligation which the law casts on them is that they should not act on any information which they may receive unless they put it to the party against whom it is to be used and give him a fair opportunity to explain it. What is a fair opportunity depend on the facts and circumstances of each case but where such an opportunity has been given, the proceedings are not open to attack on the ground that the enquiry was not conducted in accordance with the procedure followed in courts." Reference may also be made to observations in Ranu Bala Paul & Others vs. Bani Chakraborty 1999 ACJ 634 Gauhati wherein the claim was allowed after consideration of FIR before the Tribunal. In N.K.V. Bros. (P) Ltd. v. M. Marumai Ammal, 1980 ACJ 435 (SC), the Supreme Court pointed out that the Accidents Claims Tribunal must take special care to see that innocent victims do not suffer and persons liable do not escape liability merely because of some doubt here and some obscurity there. The court should not succumb to niceties, technicalities and mystic maybes. There is no dispute on the proposition of law that simple involvement of vehicle in accident cannot make respondent liable to pay compensation unless rash and negligent driving is proved, as referred in Lachoo Ram & Ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation 2014 (1) TAC 724 SC which is relied upon by counsel for insurance company. Further, there is no dispute on the proposition that FIR may not be conclusive proof of such negligence and relevance of FIR may be limited to see whether the accident and injuries had taken place at all as held in National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Islavath Chinnamma & Ors. IV 2006 ACC 843 referred by counsel for insurance company. It was also contended that petitioner is not entitled to any loss of income during the period of treatment. It was also held that the contention of the respondents that there was no loss of earning capacity since there was a gradual increase in income as reflected from the Income Tax Returns is misconceived. In The National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Dr. Ashok Raikar (supra), the assessment of the income by the Tribunal on the basis of average income for three years was not interferred in appeal and it was also held that grant of compensation on account of permanent disability will not disentitle the injured to claim compensation for complete loss of earning for the period of 11 months of the period of treatment. In ICICI Lombard Motor Insurance Company Ltd. and Another Vs. Santosh Verma @ Santosh Soni and Another 2013 (101) ALR 630 (High Court of Allahabad), the Hon'ble High Court took the average of the three years income as per the Income Tax Returns for the purpose of assessment of income. The petitioner who was doing the job of goldsmith and had suffered 80% permanent disability was further held to be entitled for claim for future prospects on the ground of increase of income over the years. In Suraj Verma Vs. Sangeeta Chhabra & Ors. 2012 (132) DRJ 134 (Delhi High Court), the Hon'ble High Court granted to the appellant who was a Class A government contractor an addition of 30% towards the future prospects/inflation as he became quadriplegic on account of injuries suffered in the accident without any chances of recovery on the basis of income as assessed in Income Tax Returns. In Vimal Kanwar and Ors. Vs. Kishore Dan and Ors. AIR 2013 SC 3830, the Hon'ble Supreme Court after referring to the other judgements on the issue held that the deceased who was a salaried person was entitled for 100% increase in future income for the purpose of assessment of compensation. The same comes to Rs. 5,07,113.33 per annum [i.e. Rs.6,25,033/- (AY 2008-09) + Rs. 4,44,087/- (AY 2009-10) + Rs.4,52,220/- (AY 2010-11) divided by 3] or Rs.42,259.44 per month. In Concord of India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Smt. Nirmala Devi & Ors. MANU/SC/0384/1979 : 1979 (4) SCC 365, the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that the determination of compensation must be liberal, not niggardly since the law values life and limb in a free country in generous scales. In Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Ram Prasad Varma & Ors. MANU / , the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that the expression 'just' must be given its logical meaning. Though, the compensation Shri Chander Mohan Sachdeva vs Shri Chanda Babu on 30 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58035091/ 9 awarded cannot be a bonanza or a source of profit but in considering as to what would be just and equitable, all facts and circumstances must be taken into consideration. (c) Functional Disability Counsel for petitioner urged that for purpose of assessment of compensation, functional disability may be considered at 24% as assessed by the Medical Board as per Disability Certificate Ex.PW1/11. On the other hand, counsel for insurance company contended that functional disability of the petitioner be assessed at 12% considering the nature of disability qua the entire body and further reliance is further placed upon Rajesh Kumar @ Raju Vs. Yudhvir Singh & Anr. IV 2008 ACC 354 SC. Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has elucidated with an example that if the left hand of claimant, who is driver by profession is amputated, the actual loss of earning capacity may be virtually 100%. The observations of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar, (supra) whereby the methodology for determining the functional disability as discussed in paragraph 14 may be quoted:- Shri Chander Mohan Sachdeva vs Shri Chanda Babu on 30 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58035091/ 10 "14. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps. In view of Sarla Verma & Ors. v/s Delhi Transport Corporation 2009, ACJ 1298, the relevant multiplier of 15 is applicable for the purpose of assessment in the present case. Medicines and Medical Treatment Counsel for petitioner contended that an amount of Rs. 4,40,294/- has been claimed towards the medical bills/treatment by the petitoiner and an amount of Rs.2,02,950/- had been reimbursed by East West TPA Pvt. Ltd. in view of the mediclaim policy obtained by the petitioner. It was further claimed that the entire amount of Rs.4,40,294/- be reimbursed to the petitioner placing reliance uopn National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Sh. Aman Kapur & Ors. 2014 ACJ 1342 and Dr. A.C. Mehra Vs. Behari Lal and Anr. I (1997) ACC 657. On the other hand, the contentions were refuted by counsel for insurance company and it was submitted that the amount which already stands reimbursed on the basis of medical claim policy, can not be again paid in compensation. . IV (2012) ACC 383 and IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Shambhu Pathak & Ors. (i) Attendant Charges Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in DTC V/s Lalit AIR 1981 Delhi 558 held that the victim is entitled to compensation even if no attendant is hired as some family member renders gratuitous services. Further, in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Rama Swamy and Others 2012 (2) T.A.C. 34 (Del.), value of gratuitous services rendered by family member of the claimant was assessed at Rs.2,000/- per month. I am of the considered view that even if the gratuitous services were rendered by some or the other family members, the claimant cannot be deprived of its benefit on the gain of the tortfeasor.
